<reason>A's case rested on a headline arithmetic claim — no surcharge for refusing means no fundable discount, so the motion "quietly abolishes" telematics [A1.1] — plus a safety impact and a strong reframe that the real alternative to behaviour pricing is ZIP-code identity pricing with no right of reply. B dismantled the headline claim in two steps: first that a real safety benefit funds its own discount from the monitored pool's own losses [B2.2], then, under direct pressure, by clarifying that its rule permits the unmonitored pool's rate to rise on observed claims experience and bans only a surcharge loaded onto refusal itself before any evidence [B4.1, B4.3]. That forced A to retreat from "abolition" to "it's only a lag," which concedes voluntary telematics survives the motion and shrinks the clash to the single clause B wanted. B also converted A's own concession that sorting, not behaviour change, is the "bigger and faster" saving [A2.1] into a clean weighing hit — "sorting saves no lives; it moves money" — blunting A's crash-victim framing, which was A's main external impact. B's concession-harvesting (A adopting resale bans, secondary-use bans, location-scoring bans, behaviour-only factors, rate review) genuinely narrowed and clarified the decision. A's best counters were real and well delivered — that B ends up pricing the nurse on "the average loss of everyone else who also refused," i.e. group averaging in a behavioural costume [A4.4-A4.5], and the closing reductio that if any price difference for withheld information is a fine, all underwriting is coercion [A5.1] — but B pre-empted the latter with a defensible in-kind distinction (a claims-history document versus a permanent record of every stop [B5.5]), and A never fully killed the surviving primary-use harms (breach/subpoena exposure, chill, proxy scoring) that answered its own Q2. Both sides handled Q/A format correctly and both had clipped turns, so execution costs offset. B built the cleaner, better-defended path.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's A1 in Rebuttal 2 [B4.1/B4.3]: distinguishing an experience-rated increase for the unmonitored pool (permitted) from a presumptive surcharge on refusal before any claim (banned) defused A's central "unfundable discount / mandated cross-subsidy" argument and forced A down to "it's just a lag." Paired with B's pressure question turning A's own "sorting is the bigger and faster saving" concession into "sorting saves no lives; it moves money," this pair of hits stripped A of both its abolition claim and its safety impact.</best_rebuttal>
